[2024 summer phd math-stat — problem 2]

Part I, Problem 2 (MLE and One-step Estimator). Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be i.i.d. with density $p_\theta(\cdot)$, regularity conditions satisfied.
1. Define the MLE and prove its asymptotic limiting distribution (you may assume consistency of the MLE).
2. State the one-step estimator and prove it has the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE.

response.text:
Let the true parameter be \(\theta_0\in\Theta\subset\mathbb R^d\), with \(\theta_0\) an interior point. Write

\[
\ell_n(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n \ell_\theta(X_i),\qquad \ell_\theta(x)=\log p_\theta(x),
\]

\[
U_n(\theta)=\nabla_\theta \ell_n(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n \dot\ell_\theta(X_i),
\]

and

\[
H_n(\theta)=\nabla_\theta^2 \ell_n(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^n \ddot\ell_\theta(X_i).
\]

Let

\[
I(\theta_0)=\mathbb E_{\theta_0}\big[\dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X)\dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X)^\top\big]
= -\mathbb E_{\theta_0}\big[\ddot\ell_{\theta_0}(X)\big]
\]

be the Fisher information matrix, assumed nonsingular. All limits below are under \(P_{\theta_0}\).

We assume the usual regularity conditions: differentiability in a neighborhood of \(\theta_0\), interchange of differentiation and integration, a uniform law of large numbers for the Hessian, and the CLT for the score.

---

## 1. MLE and its asymptotic limiting distribution

The likelihood and log-likelihood are

\[
L_n(\theta)=\prod_{i=1}^n p_\theta(X_i),\qquad \ell_n(\theta)=\log L_n(\theta).
\]

The maximum likelihood estimator is any measurable maximizer

\[
\widehat\theta_n \in \arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta} L_n(\theta)
= \arg\max_{\theta\in\Theta} \ell_n(\theta).
\]

Assume \(\widehat\theta_n\to_p \theta_0\). Since \(\theta_0\) is an interior point and \(\widehat\theta_n\to_p\theta_0\), with probability tending to \(1\), \(\widehat\theta_n\) lies in the interior of \(\Theta\). Hence the first-order condition holds:

\[
U_n(\widehat\theta_n)=0.
\]

By Taylor expansion of the score around \(\theta_0\),

\[
0
=
U_n(\widehat\theta_n)
=
U_n(\theta_0)
+
\left\{\int_0^1 H_n\big(\theta_0+t(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)\big)\,dt\right\}
(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0).
\]

Define

\[
A_n
=
\frac1n \int_0^1 H_n\big(\theta_0+t(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)\big)\,dt.
\]

Then

\[
0
=
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
+
A_n\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0),
\]

so

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)
=
-A_n^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0).
\]

Now, by the multivariate CLT,

\[
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
=
\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n \dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X_i)
\Rightarrow N_d(0,I(\theta_0)).
\]

Also, by the uniform law of large numbers for the Hessian and consistency of \(\widehat\theta_n\),

\[
A_n \to_p -I(\theta_0).
\]

Therefore, by the continuous mapping theorem and Slutsky’s theorem,

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)
=
-A_n^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
\Rightarrow
I(\theta_0)^{-1}Z,
\]

where \(Z\sim N_d(0,I(\theta_0))\). Hence

\[
I(\theta_0)^{-1}Z \sim N_d(0,I(\theta_0)^{-1}).
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0)
\Rightarrow
N_d\big(0,I(\theta_0)^{-1}\big).
}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\widehat\theta_n
=
\theta_0
+
I(\theta_0)^{-1}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X_i)
+
o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\]

---

## 2. One-step estimator and its asymptotic distribution

Let \(\widetilde\theta_n\) be a preliminary estimator satisfying

\[
\sqrt n(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0)=O_p(1).
\]

Define the observed information matrix

\[
J_n(\theta)=-\frac1n H_n(\theta)
=
-\frac1n\nabla_\theta^2\ell_n(\theta).
\]

The one-step estimator is the result of applying one Newton-Raphson step to the likelihood score equation, starting from \(\widetilde\theta_n\):

\[
\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}
=
\widetilde\theta_n
-
\{H_n(\widetilde\theta_n)\}^{-1}U_n(\widetilde\theta_n).
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}
=
\widetilde\theta_n
+
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}\frac1n U_n(\widetilde\theta_n).
\]

We prove that

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
\Rightarrow
N_d(0,I(\theta_0)^{-1}),
\]

the same limiting distribution as the MLE.

Let

\[
a_n=\sqrt n(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0)=O_p(1).
\]

Taylor expand \(U_n(\widetilde\theta_n)\) around \(\theta_0\):

\[
U_n(\widetilde\theta_n)
=
U_n(\theta_0)
+
\left\{\int_0^1 H_n\big(\theta_0+t(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0)\big)\,dt\right\}
(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\widetilde\theta_n)
=
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
+
B_n a_n,
\]

where

\[
B_n
=
\frac1n\int_0^1 H_n\big(\theta_0+t(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0)\big)\,dt.
\]

Because \(\widetilde\theta_n\to_p\theta_0\), the uniform LLN for the Hessian gives

\[
B_n\to_p -I(\theta_0).
\]

Also,

\[
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)
=
-\frac1n H_n(\widetilde\theta_n)
\to_p I(\theta_0),
\]

so

\[
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}\to_p I(\theta_0)^{-1}.
\]

Now compute

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
=
\sqrt n(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_0)
+
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\widetilde\theta_n).
\]

Substituting the Taylor expansion,

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
=
a_n
+
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}
\left\{
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
+
B_n a_n
\right\}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
=
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
+
\left[I_d+J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}B_n\right]a_n.
\]

Now

\[
J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}\to_p I(\theta_0)^{-1},
\qquad
B_n\to_p -I(\theta_0),
\]

so

\[
I_d+J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}B_n
\to_p
I_d-I_d
=
0.
\]

Since \(a_n=O_p(1)\),

\[
\left[I_d+J_n(\widetilde\theta_n)^{-1}B_n\right]a_n=o_p(1).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
=
I(\theta_0)^{-1}\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
+
o_p(1).
\]

By the multivariate CLT,

\[
\frac1{\sqrt n}U_n(\theta_0)
\Rightarrow
N_d(0,I(\theta_0)).
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0)
\Rightarrow
N_d\big(0,I(\theta_0)^{-1}\big).
}
\]

This is the same limiting distribution as the MLE. In fact, we have the stronger asymptotic equivalence

\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\widehat\theta_n)=o_p(1),
\]

because both estimators have the same asymptotic linear representation:

\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_0
=
I(\theta_0)^{-1}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X_i)
+
o_p(n^{-1/2}),
\]

and

\[
\widehat\theta_n^{(1)}-\theta_0
=
I(\theta_0)^{-1}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dot\ell_{\theta_0}(X_i)
+
o_p(n^{-1/2}).
\]

Thus the one-step estimator is asymptotically efficient and has the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE.
